title: CAT 2024 Question Paper (Slot 2, QA) - Quant - Combinatorics
subject: Quant

questions.q: P, Q, R and S are four towns. One can travel between P and Q along 3 direct paths, between Q and S along 4 direct paths, and between P and R along 4 direct paths. There is no direct path between P and S, while there are few direct paths between Q and R, and between R and S. One can travel from P to S either via Q, or via R, or via Q followed by R, respectively, in exactly 62 possible ways. One can also travel from Q to R either directly, or via P, or via S, in exactly 27 possible ways. Then, the number of direct paths between Q and R is
questions.explain: Let number of paths be $n(X,Y)$. Given $n(P,Q)=3, n(Q,S)=4, n(P,R)=4$. Let $n(Q,R)=x, n(R,S)=y$. Total ways P to S: $n(P,Q)n(Q,S) + n(P,R)n(R,S) + n(P,Q)n(Q,R)n(R,S) = 62$. So $3(4) + 4y + 3xy = 62 \implies 12 + 4y + 3xy = 62 \implies 4y+3xy=50 \implies y(4+3x)=50$. Ways Q to R: $n(Q,R) + n(Q,P)n(P,R) + n(Q,S)n(S,R) = 27$. So $x + 3(4) + 4y=27 \implies x+4y=15 \implies 4y=15-x$. Substitute: $(15-x)/4 \times (4+3x) = 50$ is not right. Let's re-read. Oh, Q to S, then S to R. $n(S,R)=y$. $x + 3(4) + 4y=27$ seems right. From $y(4+3x)=50$, $y=50/(4+3x)$. Sub into the second: $x + 4(50/(4+3x)) = 15 \implies x(4+3x)+200=15(4+3x) \implies 3x^2+4x+200=60+45x \implies 3x^2-41x+140=0$. Using quadratic formula, $x = (41 \pm \sqrt{41^2-4(3)(140)})/6 = (41 \pm \sqrt{1681-1680})/6 = (41 \pm 1)/6$. So $x=42/6=7$ or $x=40/6$ (not integer). Thus $x=7$.
